rules.citation: General Law - Part I, Title VII, Chapter 40P, Section 4
rules.title: General prohibition; exception
rules.requirement: Massachusetts generally prohibits cities and towns from enacting, maintaining, or enforcing rent control. A city or town that accepts Chapter 40P may adopt only a limited voluntary rent-control regulation meeting the statute’s conditions.
rules.key_value: Local rent control prohibited except voluntary regulation under Chapter 40P

coverage.small_owner_exception: Any permitted local rent-control regulation may not apply to a rental unit owned by a person or entity owning less than ten rental units.
coverage.other_unresolvable: Any permitted local rent-control regulation also may not apply to a rental unit with a fair market rent exceeding $400.
coverage.summary: Applies statewide to city or town rent-control regulation, with only the limited Chapter 40P exception for municipalities that accept the chapter.

rules.exemptions: A city or town accepting Chapter 40P may adopt rent control only if, after six months from initial adoption, owner compliance is entirely voluntary and uncoerced; the regulation does not regulate occupancy, services, evictions, condominium conversion, or removal of properties; it does not apply to owners with fewer than ten rental units or units with fair market rent over $400; and the municipality compensates owners for the difference between fair market rent and controlled rent from general funds.
rules.interaction: The section bars municipal rent control unless the municipality accepts Chapter 40P and follows the statute’s limited exception.
